thread:
Maria C.: Heads-up — I'm proposing gpupool module v3 that changes how we surface KMS/IAM and capacity. Main changes: split 'capacity' into 'static' + 'burst', and replace the single kms_key param with a region->alias map so teams can point to existing keys without us creating keys in every account. Will break some outward-facing inputs and may cause plan diffs for a few customers.
Sam H.: Can you paste the tf var change? curious how big the drift will look.
Maria C.: Sure — high level:
```
# before
variable "kms_key" { type = string }
# after
variable "kms_key_map" { type = map(string) }
```
We also stop creating aws_kms_key in the module. Instead we resolve aliases via data sources, so existing aliases must exist beforehand. That avoids accidental key creation across accounts.
Ben R.: That sounds safe but what about existing installs where they passed a literal arn? tf will want to replace aliases with data lookups and could try to delete resources if we had created them previously.
Maria C.: Good catch. Migration plan: 1) Add compat wrapper in v2.1 that accepts both `kms_key` and `kms_key_map` and populates `kms_key_map` from `kms_key` for now. 2) Run a dry-run migration in a canary account (eu-west-1, small gpufleet) 3) After validating, release v3 that removes wrapper. The compat wrapper avoids any resource replace/delete in a single apply.
Tony L.: How does GitOps handle this? Our auto-apply will see a non-empty plan and might apply across all clusters.
Ben R.: We'll gate via the gitops pipeline. Proposal: add a canary label to the module version in the manifests repo and conditionally point only eu-west-1 cluster at the new ref. Use the same approach as we did for the az-affinity test last quarter.
Maria C.: Exactly. Also adding an acceptance test that runs `terraform plan` and asserts zero deletes for KMS/iam resources. If plan contains deletes, pipeline fails and posts to #eng-infra.
infra-oncall: Please schedule the change during the low traffic window for eu-west-1 (Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC). Also include runbook steps to rollback module ref in gitops if things go sideways.
Sam H.: What about tfstate lock/key issues across accounts? The migration needs to be per-account because aliases are account-scoped.
Maria C.: We'll run the migration per-account via our pipeline task that assumes role into each account. Plan-only first, then apply for the canary account. For bulk accounts we will stage rollout and watch metrics.
Ben R.: Cost note — splitting static/burst allows us to cap reserved capacity and reduce steady-state spend. We should add an overlay that sets burst pools as spot by default.
Tony L.: Agree. Add an env var toggle `gpupool_v3_force_spot_burst` for the release so teams can opt-in before we flip defaults.
Maria C.: I'll add the toggle and the compat wrapper PR. PR will include a migration checklist: update manifests, run plan in staging, run canary apply, run audit script that checks KMS aliases exist, monitor SLOs for 24h.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: gpupool-v3 -> eu-west-1. CI: running terraform plan (canary) · build/gpupool-v3/142
Sam H.: :eyes: watching the plan job.
Ben R.: If the plan shows any `-/+` for aws_kms_key or aws_iam_role, don't apply. Ping infra-oncall and open a rollback PR.
Maria C.: Understood. I'll also add a small script to convert old `kms_key` strings into `kms_key_map` entries and commit a migration mapping as a one-off in the manifests repo for customers who rely on literal ARNs.
infra-oncall: Also include a note in the runbook about KMS alias rotation — if a customer rotates an alias to a new target_key_id, our data lookup will pick the new key automatically but plan might show drift; ensure we have monitoring on plan diffs.
Tony L.: Fine. One more ask: add versioned changelog in the module registry showing compat wrapper and removal timeline.
Maria C.: Will do. Timeline: PR tomorrow, canary next Wed, broad rollout over two weeks. I'll post the PR link once ready.
Ben R.: Thanks — ping if you need help with canary infra.
Maria C.: Thanks all :thumbsup:
